terms.definition: A frame of known area used to sample plants or slow-moving animals.
terms.examiner: Give the type (open frame, grid or point) and what is recorded: number, species present or percentage cover.

terms.definition: A line across a habitat along which samples are taken.
terms.examiner: Line, belt or continuous transects show how species change along an environmental gradient.

terms.definition: A container sunk level with the soil surface to catch invertebrates moving over the ground.
terms.examiner: A cover keeps out rain and predators; traps should be emptied regularly.

terms.definition: Apparatus that uses light and heat above a soil or leaf litter sample to drive invertebrates down into a collecting pot.
terms.examiner: Standardise the sample volume, the lamp distance and the time.

terms.definition: Disturbing the stream bed upstream of a net for a set time so that invertebrates are carried into it.
terms.examiner: Standardise the area disturbed and the time; a Surber sampler gives a fixed area.

terms.definition: An estimate of population size from mark, release and recapture: (number in first sample × number in second sample) ÷ number of marked animals recaptured.
terms.examiner: Assumes marks do not affect survival, the marked animals mix fully, and there is no migration, birth or death between samples.

terms.definition: A measure of biodiversity that takes account of both the number of species and the number of individuals of each.
terms.examiner: A higher value means greater diversity and usually a more stable ecosystem.

terms.definition: A black and white disc lowered into water until it can no longer be seen, to measure turbidity.
terms.examiner: The depth of disappearance is the measurement: the shallower it is, the more turbid the water.
